tagline: Credentials in minutes; reading mail needs restricted-scope verification plus an annual paid CASA security assessment
tier_reason: Any external app that reads or modifies mail (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata) uses restricted scopes. To serve more than 100 users it must pass brand verification, restricted-scope verification with a demo video, and a third-party CASA security assessment that repeats every 12 months. A send-only app (gmail.send) is sensitive, not restricted, and skips CASA. Testing mode and Internal (same Workspace org) apps need no review.

time.active_effort: 3-8 h for setup, policy pages and demo video; add 1-4 days of hands-on work for CASA scanning and fixes if you need restricted scopes
time.wait: None for Testing/Internal; about 3-10 business days for sensitive-only (gmail.send); usually 3-8 weeks for restricted scopes with CASA (anecdotal; can run longer)
time.summary: We can test with up to 100 named users today, but letting the public read their Gmail through our agent requires Google's restricted-scope review and a paid security assessment, so plan on roughly 1-2 months and a yearly renewal.

composio.note: Composio's managed-auth page lists Gmail among the toolkits that ship with managed auth. With it, users see Composio's name on the consent screen and share Composio's quota. Use your own OAuth app when you need your own branding, custom scopes, or your own quota.

oauth.pkce: Supported (S256). Not required for confidential web clients. Not confirmed by probe this session.
oauth.refresh_tokens: Add access_type=offline (plus prompt=consent to get one again) to receive a refresh token. In Testing status, test-user grants and their refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent, unless only basic profile/email/openid scopes are requested. In production, refresh tokens last until revoked, the password changes for Gmail scopes, or they sit unused for months.
oauth.scopes_note: Gmail scope classes per Google's scope table: gmail.send is Sensitive. gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, gmail.insert, gmail.settings.basic and https://mail.google.com/ are Restricted. gmail.labels is Non-sensitive.
oauth.account_needed: A free Google account with Google Cloud access. To publish you need a domain you own (verified in Google Search Console), a public homepage, and a privacy policy on that domain. An Internal app needs a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.

start_here: Decide your scopes first. If your agent only sends mail, use gmail.send (sensitive, no CASA). If it reads mail, budget for restricted-scope verification and CASA, then create a dedicated production Cloud project in Google Auth Platform.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes and confirm whether an exception applies
steps.detail:
Map every agent feature to a scope using Google's Gmail scope table.
- **Sensitive:** `gmail.send` (send only).
- **Restricted:** `gmail.readonly`, `gmail.modify`, `gmail.compose`, `gmail.metadata`, `gmail.insert`, `gmail.settings.basic`, `https://mail.google.com/`.
- **Non-sensitive:** `gmail.labels`.

Verification is not required for personal use under 100 users, Testing projects, Internal apps (same Workspace org) or admin-trusted installs. Google rejects requests for scopes held for future features, so request only what you ship.
steps.agent_help: Map tool actions to the minimal scope set; draft a per-scope justification explaining why a narrower scope won't work.

steps.title: Get a verified domain, homepage and privacy policy in place
steps.agent_help: Draft privacy-policy sections covering Google user data and the Limited Use disclosure; check that the homepage and policy URLs are public and on the same domain.

steps.title: Create a production Cloud project, enable the Gmail API, configure Google Auth Platform
steps.detail:
1. In Google Cloud console, create a project used only for production (Google asks you to keep dev/test in separate projects).
2. **APIs & Services > Library** → enable **Gmail API**.
3. **Google Auth Platform > Branding**: app name, user support email, logo, app homepage, privacy policy, terms link, **Authorized domains**, developer contact email.
4. **Audience**: User type **External** (or **Internal** if only your own Workspace org will use it). Publishing status starts at **Testing**.
5. **Data Access**: add the exact scopes you chose.
steps.agent_help: Prepare every form value (name, URLs, support email, scope list) to paste.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client and register Composio's redirect URI
steps.detail: **Google Auth Platform > Clients > Create client** → Application type **Web application**. Under **Authorized redirect URIs**, add exactly `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback`, or your own 302-proxy URL if you white-label. Copy the Client ID and secret into a Composio auth config for the Gmail toolkit, with **use your own developer credentials** enabled. If you use your own proxy domain, it must be an authorized domain you have verified.
steps.agent_help: Generate the Composio auth-config payload; compare the registered URI to Composio's character by character.

steps.title: Test in Testing mode with listed test users
steps.detail: Add test users under **Audience > Test users** (maximum 100, and each one counts against the quota once added). Run the Composio connect flow. Expect the unverified-app warning; testers click through **Advanced**. In Testing status, grants and refresh tokens expire **7 days** after consent, so connected accounts will break weekly. That is expected and is not a bug in your code.
steps.agent_help: Run the connect flow, call a Gmail action (for example, list messages), and record any OAuth errors.

steps.title: Brand verification, then publish to In production
steps.detail: In **Google Auth Platform > Branding**, submit for brand verification. The automated check often finishes in minutes, but takes 2-3 business days if branding has changed. A passing result is valid for 7 days, so publish within that window. Then go to **Audience > Publish app**. You cannot edit branding while verification is in progress unless you cancel it.

steps.title: Submit data-access (scope) verification with justification and demo video
steps.wait: Sensitive: typically 3-5 business days; restricted: several weeks
steps.detail: In the **Verification Center**, declare every scope, add up to three documentation links, and write a justification for each scope. Upload an **unlisted YouTube** demo video in English. It must show the full OAuth flow, the consent screen with your app name, the browser address bar with your **client ID**, and each feature that uses each scope. If user data trains AI models, the video must show users explicitly opting in. Watch the developer contact inbox: Trust & Safety sends follow-ups by email.
steps.agent_help: Draft the scope justifications and the demo-video shot list and script; check the video against Google's checklist.

steps.title: Pass the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: Once the other checks pass, Google's Trust & Safety team emails you to start the App Defense Alliance **CASA** assessment, which is based on OWASP ASVS. Google assigns an assurance level (AL1/AL2, commonly called Tier 2/Tier 3) from risk signals such as user count and scopes. **You choose and pay** an authorized assessor. Published vendor prices run from about $540-$720 for Tier 2 and a few thousand dollars for Tier 3 (vendor-listed, not Google-stated). Passing earns a Letter of Validation (LOV). It must be **renewed every 12 months** with a full reassessment, and adding a new restricted scope may trigger one.
steps.agent_help: Run the self-scan tooling, triage findings, and draft the questionnaire answers; the human signs and pays.
steps.evidence_note: Process, annual renewal and AL levels are from Google; prices and turnaround are from vendor and community pages and change often.

steps.title: Launch and help Workspace customers allowlist the app
steps.detail: After approval, the unverified screen and the 100-user cap go away for the approved scopes. Customers on Google Workspace may still block you. If their admin restricts Gmail under **Security > Access and data control > API controls**, untrusted apps asking for high-risk Gmail scopes are blocked and their tokens are revoked. Send admins your **OAuth client ID** so they can add it under **Manage third-party app access > Add app > OAuth App Name or Client ID** and mark it **Trusted**. Set a calendar reminder for the CASA renewal.
steps.agent_help: Write the admin allowlisting instructions to send customers.

requirements.title: Restricted scopes require a CASA security assessment
requirements.detail: Reading or modifying mail (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, https://mail.google.com/) is restricted. Restricted data accessed through your servers requires a CASA assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor, renewed every 12 months.
requirements.applies_when: External app in production with restricted Gmail scopes and more than 100 users

requirements.title: gmail.send is sensitive, not restricted
requirements.detail: A send-only agent needs sensitive-scope verification (justification and demo video) but no CASA assessment.

requirements.title: 100-user lifetime cap while unverified
requirements.detail: Apps showing the unverified-app screen can onboard 100 new users in total over the project's lifetime, and the count cannot be reset. Testing mode separately limits you to 100 listed test users.
requirements.applies_when: Sensitive or restricted scopes before verification

requirements.title: 7-day token expiry in Testing
requirements.detail: Test-user authorizations, including refresh tokens, expire 7 days after consent, unless the app requests only name, email and profile scopes.

requirements.title: Verified domain, homepage and same-domain privacy policy
requirements.detail: Every authorized domain must be verified in Search Console by a project Owner or Editor. The homepage must describe the app and link the privacy policy, which must sit on the same domain and match the link on the consent screen.

requirements.title: English demo video on unlisted YouTube
requirements.detail: The video must show the OAuth grant, the consent screen with your app name, the client ID in the address bar, and the use of each scope.

requirements.title: Limited Use policy
requirements.detail: Gmail data may only be used for user-facing features. Ads, sale and most human reading are forbidden, and AI-training use needs explicit user consent shown in the demo video.

requirements.title: Gmail API quotas
requirements.detail: Per Google's quota page: 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project and 6,000 per user per project per minute, for projects created on or after 1 May 2026. messages.send costs 100 units, messages.get 20 (60 for full/raw formats), messages.list 5.

blockers.title: Google hasn't verified this app
blockers.symptom: Users see an unverified-app warning and must click Advanced to continue.
blockers.what_to_do: Expected in Testing or before verification. Add the people testing as test users. For production, finish brand and scope verification.

blockers.title: 101st user is refused
blockers.symptom: New users can't authorize once the unverified app has reached 100 users, or anyone not on the test-user list is refused while in Testing.
blockers.what_to_do: The lifetime cap can't be reset. Complete verification, or move internal users to an Internal app in your Workspace org.
blockers.evidence_note: The cap is sourced; the exact error text shown to the 101st user was not observed.

blockers.title: invalid_grant after about a week
blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with invalid_grant ('Token has been expired or revoked') about 7 days after connecting.
blockers.what_to_do: This is the Testing-mode 7-day expiry. Publish to In production; testers can reconnect in the meantime.

blockers.title: redirect_uri_mismatch
blockers.symptom: Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch on the Google sign-in page.
blockers.what_to_do: Register exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (or your proxy URL) on the Web client, with no trailing slash. The URI in the Composio auth config must match it.
blockers.evidence_note: Standard Google OAuth behaviour; not probed this session because the authorize endpoint was blocked by the research network.

blockers.title: Workspace admin blocks the app
blockers.symptom: Workspace users are told the app is blocked by their admin, or existing tokens are revoked.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to mark your client ID as Trusted under API controls.

blockers.title: Verification rejected for over-broad scopes
blockers.symptom: Trust & Safety asks why a narrower scope won't work, or rejects https://mail.google.com/ or gmail.modify.
blockers.what_to_do: Drop to the narrowest scope (for example, gmail.readonly + gmail.send) and rewrite the justification per feature.

ready_to_paste.note: From Composio's white-labeling docs (confirmed 2026-10-28). Use your own 302-proxy URL instead if you white-label the domain.

ready_to_paste.note: gmail.readonly is restricted (CASA needed); gmail.send alone is sensitive.

ready_to_paste.label: App description
ready_to_paste.value: <AppName> is an AI assistant that, at the user's request, reads and summarizes their Gmail messages and drafts or sends replies on their behalf. Data is used only to provide these user-facing features and is never used for advertising or sold.

ready_to_paste.label: Scope justification template
ready_to_paste.value: Scope: <scope>. Feature: <user-facing feature>. Why it is needed: <what the user triggers and what data is touched>. Why a narrower scope is insufficient: <e.g. gmail.metadata lacks message bodies needed to summarize; gmail.send cannot read the thread being replied to>. Storage: <retention, encryption, deletion on request>.

Matches the guide.
